scenes.headline: How a font file shrinks to a tenth
scenes.sub: And how to prove nothing moved
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Hairline! Let me show you how a web font gets small without changing a pixel.

scenes.text: Keep only the characters, features and weights a site really uses, then compare pixels to prove that nothing moved.
scenes.say: Keep only the characters, features and weights the site really uses. Then compare pixels, to prove that nothing moved.

scenes.title: One big file becomes two small ones

steps.say: Wrapping the font in WOFF2 compresses it, and changes no pixel.
Subsetting then keeps only the characters the pages print.
The common characters go into a small core file, which is preloaded.
The rest wait in an extended file, fetched only when a page needs one of them.

scenes.title: Two ways to ship a font

left.title: The whole font
left.say: The usual way ships every glyph and every weight, in one big download.

right.title: What the site prints
items: A core file for most pages
An extra file only when needed
right.say: This way ships a core for most pages, and an extra file only when a page needs it.

scenes.title: How the proof works
scenes.say: Every rung gets the same test.

items.say: Render the same text with the old font and the new one.
Subtract the two images, pixel by pixel.
Explain every pixel that differs, or undo the step.

scenes.title: Inter, rung by rung
scenes.say: For Inter, each rung takes bytes away. The core file ends at thirty thousand, down from three hundred and fifty thousand.

scenes.label: of articles still need the extended file
scenes.note: with the prompt's own core, on this site
scenes.say: But a core is only as good as its character list. On this site, most pages still need the extra file.

scenes.text: Subsetting changed no pixel. Dropping features and trimming weights each need an approval, and the core must be measured.
scenes.say: Subsetting alone changed no pixel. Features and weights need a person's approval, and the core list has to be measured.
Compress, subset, split into a core and an extra, and diff every step.
